Welcome to Boone County, Missouri
Boone County was founded in 1820 by settlers moving westward from Kentucky, Tennessee, and Virginia. These pioneers were drawn to the area's rolling foothills, wide open prairies and scenic bluffs overlooking the Missouri river. Originally known as Boone's Lick Country, the settlement was named for the nearby salt lick operated by Daniel Boone's sons.
In 1839, Boone County became home to the ﬁrst Land Grant University established west of the Mississippi. Today, Boone County sits at the crossroads of major highways and is a regional hub for commerce, healthcare, and innovation. Known for its outstanding quality of life and cultural activity, Boone County continues to be one of America's most desirable places to live, work, and do business.

Oct
14
Boone County Commission to Consider Budget Amendment for Out-of-County Detainee Housing
At its October 15 meeting in Sturgeon, the Boone County Commission will consider a budget amendment to increase funding to cover the cost of out-of-county detainee housing for the remainder of 2026. Year-to-date costs for housing detainees out of county during the first three quarters of 2026 have surpassed $3.3 million with the projected total costs for 2026 to be $4.5 million.
Read More : Boone County Commission to Consider Budget Amendment for Out-of-County Detainee Housing
Oct
06
Boone County OEM Expands School Reunification Readiness
The Boone County Office of Emergency Management (BCOEM) is continuing its investment in school emergency preparedness by providing the Centralia R-VI School District and Southern Boone County R-I School District with equipment to support student reunification following a serious emergency.
Read More : Boone County OEM Expands School Reunification Readiness
Sep
24
Boone County Joint Communications Completes Next Generation 911 Network Transition
Boone County Joint Communications (BCJC) has completed the transition to a new AT&T Emergency Services IP Network (ESInet). As part of the transition, Text-to-911 service has also been restored and is available to the public.
Read More : Boone County Joint Communications Completes Next Generation 911 Network Transition
